phosphatidylinositide 4-phosphate 4-kinase isoforms α,β, and γ discriminate among substrates and activator species with different acyl chain compositions.
the three isoforms of phosphoinositide 4-phosphate 3-kinase (PI4P3K) exhibit different degrees of acyl chain selectivities in their substrate and activator preferences.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of the synthesis of phosphatidyliol phosphates in the cell.
the role played by the acyl chain composition of the substrate and the lipid activator in the activity of phosphatidyinositol-4-phospate 5-kinasses (PIP5K).
understanding the mechanisms that produce physiologically active species of phosphatidyliol 4,5 bisphosphate in cells, which is a crucial signaling lipid in many cellular processes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the three isoforms of mammalian PIP5Ks exhibit acyl chain selectivities for both substrate and lipid activator.
PIP5 kinase isoenzymes are selective for acyl chains of both the substrate and the lipid activator.

the three PIP5Ks are selective for acyl chain length and saturation in their substrates, phosphatidylinositols, and their activators, phosphatidic acids, with the γ-isoform being the most selective.

phosphatidylinositides and their lipid activators are not all equivalent in their ability to be used by the enzymes.
